24: Underwater images, during the acquisition process, are affected by light absorption and scattering effects, and generally suffer from colour imbalance, insufficient contrast and texture degradation, which severely constrain the effectiveness of advanced vision tasks such as underwater object detection. This thesis focuses on the two core tasks of underwater image super-resolution reconstruction and object detection, proposes two improved deep-learning-based methods, and validates them through systematic experiments on public datasets.
25: For underwater image super-resolution reconstruction, this thesis proposes the Frequency-Spatial Coupled Inference Network (FSCIN). The core of this network is the Spatial-Frequency Awareness Module (SFAM), which combines the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) with Swin Transformer-based spatial-domain encoding. Using a dual-branch structure, it adaptively enhances the frequency-domain amplitude component and phase component separately, then restores them to the spatial domain via the Inverse Fast Fourier Transform (IFFT), achieving deep integration of global frequency-domain information and local spatial-domain features. In addition, this thesis introduces a texture-structure joint loss function, which applies targeted constraints to the image texture layer and structure layer separately, explicitly supervising the recovery of high-frequency details and geometric edges, thereby compensating for the limitations of conventional pixel-level losses. Experiments on the public USR-248 and UFO-120 datasets show that FSCIN achieves PSNR of 30.04 dB and 25.98 dB respectively at x2 magnification, attains leading overall performance across multiple magnification factors, and delivers efficient reconstruction with only 30.70 GFLOPs and 0.55 M parameters.
26: For underwater image object detection, this thesis addresses the problems of YOLOv8 in underwater scenes - a limited local receptive field and insufficient feature representation capability for small objects - by designing a fine-grained feature extraction module to replace the original C2f module. This module is built collaboratively from three sub-modules: the Channel-Spatial Adaptive Enhancement Module precisely focuses on object edges and texture details through a channel-spatial dual attention mechanism; the Mamba-based Global Perception Module introduces a visual state space model to model global spatial dependencies with linear complexity; and the Multi-Scale Cross-Attention Fusion Module adaptively integrates local and global features through asymmetric convolution and cross-scale attention interaction. Experiments on the URPC2021 underwater object detection dataset show that, compared with the original YOLOv8, the improved model raises mAP50 by 1.8 percentage points and raises the small-object detection metric APs by 1.1 percentage points.
27: Keywords: underwater image super-resolution; frequency-spatial coupling; texture-structure loss; YOLOv8; underwater object detection
